entities.name: Inns of Court
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: The four professional associations of barristers in England — Lincoln's Inn, Gray's Inn, Inner Temple, and Middle Temple — established in the 14th century as the exclusive institutions for training and regulating lawyers. The Inns created the common law legal profession, requiring years of apprenticeship, dining rituals, and moot court practice that shaped Anglo-American legal education.
